metadata.title: Content Creation Isn't One Post for Everywhere.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude 'does content creation,' is that one piece of writing pasted everywhere, or does it change per channel? Lands the carry-out that the skill drafts six different formats, each built to its own channel's rules, from one instruction file.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes this skill just writes a blog post. It doesn't — it drafts marketing content across six channels, each formatted its own way: blog, social, email, landing pages, press releases, case studies.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This kind of writing is built from something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it works. Inside is one file, written in plain language, that spells out exactly what each channel's version needs to look like. Claude reads the file, then follows it. The file is the whole program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, references/, scripts/; SKILL.md highlighted

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal three items: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), a references/ folder, a scripts/ folder. A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written — draft the piece, fit it to the channel's format, then return the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Three-phase pipeline: Read SKILL.md -> Draft + fit to channel -> Return result

production_viz.label: Input in, output fit to channel
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Draft + fit to channel', 'Return result'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.narration_text: For this skill, there are exactly six formats it covers: blog posts, social media, email newsletters, landing pages, press releases, and case studies — each with its own shape, from SEO-optimized copy on a blog to a headline and a call to action on a landing page. Ask for a seventh kind of writing and there's no format that covers it.

shot.new_visual_element: Six format rows: blog, social, email, landing page, press release, case study; a boundary line with 'nothing outside this list' beyond it

production_viz.label: Exactly six formats
production_viz.mechanic: Six rows fill in one at a time with a checkmark: 'Blog post — SEO copy', 'Social media — short hook', 'Email newsletter — subject + preview', 'Landing page — headline + CTA', 'Press release — announcement shape', 'Case study — narrative proof'. A dashed boundary line beneath the list, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'nothing outside this list'.

beats.narration_text: Content creation here isn't one post copied everywhere — it's six different formats, each built to its own channel's rules, from one instruction file.

props.quote: Content creation here isn't one post copied everywhere — it's six different formats, each built to its own channel's rules, from one instruction file.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Ask Claude: I just published a new blog post about backyard composting. Give me a short social media post, a two-line email subject and preview, and one landing-page headline with a call to action — built for each channel, not the same paragraph three times. Liam, in for Bear.
